chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad, who raised it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a person afflicted with smallpox who was affected by janabah. He said: “If he caused himself to become junub, then he must perform ghusl; but if he experienced a wet dream, then he must perform tayammum.”

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became junub through his own action
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring purification
key_terms.فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: then he must perform tayammum (dry ablution)
key_terms.فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ: then he must perform ghusl (ritual bath)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person with smallpox who becomes junub?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person afflicted with smallpox who enters the state of janabah. It distinguishes between janabah resulting from one's own act and janabah resulting from a wet dream, assigning ghusl in the first case and tayammum in the second.
